_comment: Performance budgets for v10r — the SINGLE source of truth, read by both the app (src/lib/server/perf/budgets.ts) and the shell probes in scripts/perf/ (via jq). TWO kinds of threshold live here and they do different jobs. `budgets` are TARGETS: where we want to be, scored on /admin/perf, never build-failing — several are red today and that is the honest state. `ceilings` are the RATCHET: the measured value at the time it was accepted, asserted by snapshot.gate.test.ts, and they only ever move DOWN. A target you cannot meet today still tells the truth; a ratchet stops today's number becoming tomorrow's floor. Ceilings carry ~3% headroom over the measured value on purpose: set exactly at the measurement, adding one showcase page tripped the gate, and a gate that fails on ordinary work is a gate that gets muted. The headroom absorbs a feature; it does not absorb a heavy dependency, which is what this is for. Lab measurements require a production build (NODE_ENV=production) — a dev-mode build inflates client JS ~9%. Field measurements come from real-user telemetry, prod lane only.
